create.name: Kaitlin Curtice
create.bio:
Kaitlin Curtice is a writer, poet and speaker and an enrolled citizen of the Potawatomi Nation. Her books follow the way faith, identity and belonging shift over a lifetime, and ask how Indigenous ways of seeing can change how people relate to the land, to their ancestors and to each other. Native looks back on her own path as a Potawatomi woman raised within Christianity, Living Resistance offers everyday practices of rest, embodiment and remembering, and Everything Is a Story examines the narratives we inherit and how they can be retold. She has also written a series of picture books for children that follows the four seasons.

Kaitlin co-founded and directs the Aki Institute, whose work centres on rest, responsibility and resistance, and she writes The Liminality Journal on Substack. She speaks at universities, churches, festivals and conferences, and has led retreats and workshops at places such as the Chautauqua Institution and Iona Abbey in Scotland. Her Kripalu programmes mix readings from her books and poetry with journaling, mindfulness practice and conversation in small groups. She lives near Philadelphia.

books.title: Everything Is a Story: Reclaiming the Power of Stories to Heal and Shape Our Lives
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: Kaitlin's 2025 book on the stories we are handed by family, culture and faith. Drawing on Potawatomi teaching and her own life, she shows readers how to notice which stories serve them and how to tell new ones.

books.title: Living Resistance: An Indigenous Vision for Seeking Wholeness Every Day
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: A book that treats resistance as an everyday spiritual practice rather than a slogan. Moving through personal, communal, ancestral and integral realms, Kaitlin suggests small practices such as resting, listening to the body and remembering one's ancestors.

books.title: Native: Identity, Belonging, and Rediscovering God
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: Kaitlin's account of growing up Potawatomi and Christian, and of reclaiming her Indigenous identity as an adult. It reflects on belonging, the harm done to Native nations in the name of faith, and finding the sacred in her own heritage.

books.title: Glory Happening: Finding the Divine in Everyday Places
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: Kaitlin's first book, a collection of short reflections on noticing the sacred in ordinary days and places.

books.title: Winter's Gifts (An Indigenous Celebration of Nature)
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: Part of Kaitlin's illustrated series for children about the four seasons, written from a Potawatomi perspective. This volume celebrates what winter brings.

books.title: Spring's Miracles (An Indigenous Celebration of Nature)
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: A picture book in which an Indigenous girl watches the land come back to life in spring and learns about courage as one of the Creator's gifts.

books.title: Summer's Magic (An Indigenous Celebration of Nature)
books.author: Kaitlin B. Curtice
books.description: The summer volume of Kaitlin's illustrated series for children about the seasons, celebrating time outdoors and a child's bond with the natural world.

courses.title: Living Our Sacred Resistance
courses.description: A two-session online workshop with Kripalu based on Kaitlin's book Living Resistance. The first session looks at personal and community life and the second at ancestral and integral life, with mindfulness practices, journaling and small-group sharing.

courses.title: Sacred Mirrors: Honoring Powerful Stories for Ourselves, One Another, and Mother Earth
courses.description: A weekend at Kripalu in Stockbridge, Massachusetts, drawing on Indigenous wisdom and Kaitlin's book Everything Is a Story. Through readings, poetry, journaling and small-group sharing it looks at the stories we carry about ourselves, our relationships and the Earth.

courses.title: Thresholds of Alchemy
courses.description: A collection of Kaitlin's poems sold as an ebook from her website, with a download link sent after purchase. The poems reflect on change, grief and becoming.

free_resources.title: The Liminality Journal
free_resources.description: Kaitlin's newsletter on Substack, with essays and poems on Indigenous spirituality, identity and living in between. Free subscribers receive a booklet of her poems; a paid tier is also offered.

All videos are on other channels (she has none); she is the main speaker in each. The Richard Rohr conversation (Baker Publishing) is shared, but it is about her book.
